speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)

The combination of rapidly progressive dementia (forgetfulness, job loss), psychiatric symptoms (hallucinations, irritability), myoclonus (involuntary movements), and early bulbar symptoms (difficulty swallowing) in a 42-year-old is highly suggestive of a prion disease. The family history of suicide at age 50 could indicate a genetic predisposition, such as Gerstmann-Sträussler-Scheinker syndrome or familial CJD. Can you confirm if these involuntary movements are sudden muscle jerks or stiffness?
